caption:
這次訪問到的是音樂治療碩士生 Bonnie Diamond，是臺波波小夥伴的同學喔！Bonnie 說希望他未來回來看的時候不要反對自己說的話哈哈哈。
We invited Bonnie Diamond, a masters student at Lesley University studying music therapy! Bonnie hopes that she won't find herself disagreeing with what she said in this interview when she looks back on it in the future haha XD.
-
Bonnie出生於麻州，在紐約大學學習聲樂表演，並長期在音樂劇團中工作，直到COVID的發生，她在新澤西州的後院開始了一個小型音樂課，她試圖運用音樂治療技巧與孩子們互動。她找到了Lesley大學，開始了第二個職業生涯，並搬回麻州。
Bonnie is a native-born in Massachusetts. She has a background in music theatre performance and also studied vocal performance at NYU. She worked in the theater industry professionally until COVID. During this time she started a little music class in her backyard in New Jersey, using music therapy techniques with kids. She decided to come to Lesley to pursue her second career and move back to Massachusetts.

Bonnie現在在一所學校實習，她服務的對象是六年級至十二年級的不同身心疾病的青少年。她的工作涉及幫助他們完成學業和學習其他重要技能，例如社交技能、時間管理和壓力管理。這些青少年家庭生活環境不好，因此她也協助他們應對相關的壓力。雖然她以音樂為基礎與他們合作，但有時也會進行諮商以提供各種支持。
Bonnie's current internship involves assisting adolescents with mental health disabilities in a school-based setting, ranging from sixth to twelfth graders. In addition to helping them complete their education, she also teaches students’ social skills, time management, and stress management which are essential skills for adolescents. She supports students in managing stresses that we normally don’t think about such as having access to a stable home. While her work involves using music therapy techniques, she also provides talk therapy to offer support students in various ways.
-
身為一名音樂治療學生，Bonnie希望透過音樂的自然性及好玩的方式來發掘每個人獨特的優勢和資源。
As a music therapy student, Bonnie hopes to use the natural and fun nature of music to discover each individual's unique strengths and abilities.

🎵「我希望能透過好玩且不刻意的方式幫助更多人，而這就是音樂的力量」 by Bonnie
🎵“I aim to utilize the power of music to support people in a playful and effortless manner.” says Bonnie. 
-

excerpt: 今天要來分享一個我們在 1 月份採訪的美國心理諮商師、表達性藝術治療師Carolyn Melbye（第三次 Table & Therapist 採訪）所創作的活動與體驗！ Today we are going to share an activity and experiential created by Carolyn Melbye, a LMHC and Expressive Arts Therapist whom we interviewed back in January (the third Table
caption:
今天要來分享一個我們在 1 月份採訪的美國心理諮商師、表達性藝術治療師Carolyn Melbye（第三次 Table & Therapist 採訪）所創作的活動與體驗！

Today we are going to share an activity and experiential created by Carolyn Melbye, a LMHC and Expressive Arts Therapist whom we interviewed back in January (the third Table & Therapist interview)! 

這是Carolyn Melbye創作的活動，並從野獸派中汲取靈感。野獸派（法語：Les Fauves）是20世紀初期的象徵主義畫派，畫風強烈、用色大膽鮮豔，採用大膽塗色技法。畫家捨棄客觀性，偏好主觀性，拋棄對現實的直接再現。他們不再講究透視和明暗、放棄傳統的遠近比例與明暗法，採用平面化構圖、陰影面與物體面的強烈對比，脫離自然的模仿。

This is a experiential created by Carolyn Melbye, which she draws inspiration from Les Fauves, also known as” the wild beasts” in French, is a group of early 20th-century modern artists whose works emphasized painterly styles and qualities with strong, bold, and bright coloring. This abandons objectivity in favor of subjectivity, letting go direct representation of reality. They no longer pay attention to the traditional distance ratio and chiaroscuro, adopting a flat composition by creating strong contrast between shadow surface and object surface, and break away from natural imitation. 

這種體驗為失憶或失智的老年人提供了創造空間，讓他們通過藝術、記憶和對話重新建立聯繫。Carolyn用她對藝術的興趣，與自己在藝術歷史方面的背景，創造了這個體驗。此活動不僅限於老年人！

This experiential gives older adults with memory loss or dementia the creative space to regain connections through the arts, memories, and conversations. She uses her personal interest in art and her background in art history to create this experiential. This activity does not limit to older adults only!

caption:
下周就是我們的春假了，這也代表著這個學期已經過了一半了！我相信有許多朋友即將畢業進入找工作的階段，而還沒畢業的朋友也許正在思考職涯方向。今天，我想和大家分享一個與職涯發展有關的理論，希望提供一些新的方向。
Spring break is next week and we're already halfway through the semester! Many friends are about to graduate and start job hunting, while others are still figuring out their career direction. Today, I want to share a theory on career development to provide some new perspectives.

你是個喜歡計畫的人嗎？會不會對偶然事件感到焦慮呢？你有提前規劃你的職涯發展嗎？職業生涯是可以規劃的嗎？
Are you someone who likes to plan? Do you get anxious about unexpected events? Have you planned your career development in advance? Can a career be planned?

傳統職涯發展理論通常強調職業決策是理性思考和規劃的過程，忽視了偶然事件的重要性，而偶然事件則被視為「錯誤的來源」，需要盡可能減少其「負面」影響，以實現無誤差的決策。
Traditional career development theories often emphasize that career decisions are a process of rational thinking and planning, ignoring the importance of unexpected events. By minimizing the unexpected or “chance events” we can make more  accurate decisions. 

但Mitchell, Levin與Krumboltz於1999年提出「善用機緣論」 (planned happenstance theory原譯為規劃的偶發事件理論)以一個不同的角度理解偶然事件，他們希望將計劃偶然性納入職業生涯諮詢過程，以幫助來訪者應對多變的生涯世界。
In 1999, (Mitchell, Levin, and Krumboltz) proposed "planned happenstance theory" to understand chance events with a different perspective. They hoped that by incorporating planned happenstance into career counseling process that it would help people cope with the ever-changing career world.

讓我們回到文章開頭的問題：職業生涯需要提前規劃嗎？可以提前規劃嗎？
Let's revisit the article's opening question: Is planning your career in advance necessary? 

Krumboltz的回答是，他不反對規劃，只要你有所準備並且這讓你感到開心。但是，他警告不要因為是曾經的目標就苦苦堅持一份工作。隨著我們成長和周圍環境的不斷變化，我們的目標和環境也在不斷改變。因此，希望這可以幫助你保持開放的心。
Krumboltz’s answer is that he doesn't oppose planning as long as it makes you happy. However, he warns against staying in a job only because it was a goal in the past. As we grow, our goals and surroundings change constantly. So, hope this allows you to always stay open-minded!

She works with a variety of populations in various settings, including treatment facilities for adults, expressive arts studio programs for adults with autism, and nursing home settings for older adults.

caption:
你喜歡唱歌嗎？你喜歡自己的聲音嗎？我在接觸音樂治療以前，其實是不太喜歡唱歌的，甚至對自己的聲音感到有點不自在與陌生。但是開始實習以後，發現對於音樂治療師而言，能夠靈活運用自己的聲音真的好~重~要~！於是開始探索我與自己的聲音之間的關係，唱歌的開關也從此被打開，走到哪裡就可以唱到哪裡🤣
Do you like to sing? Do you like your voice? Before I got into music therapy, I actually didn’t like singing very much. I even felt a bit uncomfortable and unfamiliar with my own voice. But after starting my internship, I discovered that for music therapists, being able to flexibly use our own voice is really important! So I started to explore my relationship between myself and my own voice. Since then, my “singing switch” has been turned on, and I can sing wherever I go. 🤣

今天要介紹的活動，是Lesley音樂治療課程之一「臨床聲音(Clinical voice)」的一項聲音探索作業。這個聲音探索活動非常簡單又有趣，可以一個人進行，也可以跟親朋好友們一起玩！
The activity we will be introducing today is a vocal exploration assignment for "Clinical voice", one of Lesley’s music therapy core courses. This vocal exploration activity is very simple, interesting, and fun to do by yourself or with friends and family!

在聲音探索的過程中，也許會發現一些關於自己的驚喜喔！你有發現什麼驚喜嗎？歡迎留言和我們分享！
(我先來分享：我發現我超級喜歡邊亂叫邊唱歌的！😆)
During the vocal exploration activity, you may discover some surprises about yourself! Do you find any surprises? Please leave a comment and share with us!
(I’ll share it first: I found out that I loved screaming while singing!😆)

excerpt: 基於自然的表達性藝術療法 Nature-based Expressive Arts Therapy - 你是個喜愛花花草草，對大自然、對園藝感興趣的人嗎？觀察一下你的四周，有沒有引起你注意的自然物呢？ Are you someone who loves flowers and plants and is also interested in nature and gardening? Look around and observe your surroundings: Are there any natural o
caption:
基於自然的表達性藝術療法
Nature-based Expressive Arts Therapy
-
你是個喜愛花花草草，對大自然、對園藝感興趣的人嗎？觀察一下你的四周，有沒有引起你注意的自然物呢？
Are you someone who loves flowers and plants and is also interested in nature and gardening? Look around and observe your surroundings: Are there any natural objects that caught your attention?
-
我們今天要分享的是「基於自然的表達性藝術療法」。一種著重於探討人與自然、生態或環境關係的療法。
Today, we will be sharing with you about “Nature-Based Expressive Art Therapy,” an approach that focuses on the relationship between human and nature, ecology, or the environment.
-
簡單來說，這套理論認為自然世界可以提供一種接地感和聯繫感，這對處理情緒或心理困難的個人是有益的。同時，自然環境也可以作為靈感和創造力的源泉，幫助個人以新穎而有意義的方式表達自己。
In simple terms, this theory believes that the natural world can provide a sense of grounding and connection, benefiting individuals who are dealing with emotional or psychological difficulties. Simultaneously, the natural environment can also serve as a source of inspiration and creativity, supporting individuals to express themselves in new and meaningful ways.
-
基於自然的表達性治療師也會關注於客戶與土地和文化間的複雜關係。利用不同的藝術形式與自然結合，進行創造性表達活動，並在過程中考慮人與自然之間的關係並提出問題。
Nature-based expressive arts therapists also focus on clients' complex relationships with land and culture. They use different art forms to combine with nature, engage in creative expression activities, and in the process, consider the relationship between people and nature and ask questions about it 
-

caption:
臺波波第三次訪談文來啦！ 感謝大家的等候！
Here comes the third Table & Therapist interview! Thank you all for waiting! 

這次的訪問，我們邀請到美國心理諮商師、表達性藝術治療師Carolyn Melbye。
This time we invited and interviewed Carolyn Melbye, a LMHC and Expressive Arts Therapist. 

Carolyn 在麻省大學阿默斯特分校獲得了藝術歷史和法律研究的藝術學士、文學士雙學位。2014 年，她於萊斯利大學取得表達性藝術治療和心理諮商碩士學位後，便一直從事表達性藝術治療相關工作。
Carolyn first received her BFA and BA dual degree in Art History and Legal Studies at University of Massachusetts Amherst. She then received her Master of Arts degree in Expressive Arts Therapy and Mental Health Counseling at Lesley University in 2014 and has been practicing expressive arts therapy ever since. 

Carolyn 目前在 Elliot Community Human Services 擔任門診臨床治療師，為不同背景的個案提供門診心理健康諮商。她也在 East Boston Neighborhood Health Center、Facing Cancer Together、Great Days for Seniors、Memory cafes等機構擔任表達性藝術治療師，為不同年齡及背景的個案提供一對一治療、團體治療、諮商服務，以及父母或照顧者的支持服務。她主要的服務對象是記憶力衰退和失智症的長者們。
Carolyn is currently work at the Elliot Community Human Services as an outpatient clinician, providing outpatient mental health counseling to clients of diverse backgrounds. She also works as an expressive arts therapist at East Boston Neighborhood Health Center, Facing Cancer Together, Great Days for Seniors, Memory cafes, etc., serving clients of all ages and background with 1:1 therapy, group therapy, and parent or caregiver support. She has been working more with older adults with memory loss and dementia. 

身為一名表達性藝術治療師，Carolyn 非常重視協作、創造力、關懷和好奇心的重要性：我們如何在「此時此地」與個案同在？在這一刻，個案們怎麼從表達性藝術治療中受益？
As an expressive arts therapist, Carolyn places great emphasis on the importance of collaboration, creativity, care, and curiosity. How do we meet our clients in the here and now?  How can expressive arts therapy benefit them in this given moment? 

👂「在你下判斷之前，傾聽並保持好奇心。」By Carolyn 表達性藝術治療師
👂“Listen and be curious before you judge.” – Carolyn Melbye

今天要來分享一個大家可以從身體了解情緒的活動！不知道大家有沒有這種經驗：去到一個地方，或遇到某個人，身體會有感覺到不舒服，然後下意識的想要離開，其實啊，身體會幫我們紀錄有哪些東西適合我們、不適合我們，並且無時無刻的在提供訊息。當我們可以有意識的接收到身體的訊息，並且能做出對自己最好的回應與最真實的表達，就能夠更清楚的了解自己的情緒進而釋放掉記憶在身體裡的創傷或不再需要的舊有信念。分享給大家！ 
Today we are going to share an activity everyone can do to understand their emotions through their body! Don’t know if you all have this kind of experience: when you go to a place or meet someone, your body feels uncomfortable, and the subconsciously want to leave. In fact, the body will help us record what is best for us and what is not suitable for us. Our body continuously provides information to us all the time. When we can consciously receive our body’s messages and make the best response and most authentic expression for ourselves, we can then understand our emotions more clearly and release traumatic memories from the body, letting go of our old beliefs. Sharing this with you all! 
 
 
材料：5張紙、任何想要的話畫媒材
Materials: 5 sheets of paper, any desired drawing medium.

準備工作：想一件你最近記得深刻的事件。
Preparation work: Consider a recent event that you remember vividly. 
 
1. 先以舞蹈或動作來感受這件事，並分成三個部分：身體的、情緒的、想法，把當時的感受帶回當下。
1. Use dance or movement to feel this situation, divide it into three parts: body, emotion, and thought, and bring those feelings at that time back to the here and now.
 
 
2. 使用想要的媒材將剛剛的感受分別畫成圖像在三張紙上。
2. Use your desired medium to draw images of what you just felt on three pieces of paper. 
 
3. 將動作、舞蹈、畫畫變成文字寫在分成三等份的紙上。 
3. Turn actions, dances, and drawings into words and write them down on paper divided into three equal parts. 
 
4. 最後，停下來感受三種不同表達性藝術給你的不同想法，用最後的紙記錄、畫下任何身體上融合的感受。 
4. Finally, take a moment to feel the different inspirations/ideas each expressive art have provided you with. Use the last piece of paper to record or draw any feelings of physical interaction. 

結束了解情緒過後可以將所有的作品攤開來看。 
可以留意身體的呼吸、心跳、與作品的相關？你喜歡不喜歡的部分是什麼？ 任何其他的想法？ 
Once you have a grasp of these emotions, you may spread out all of the works for yourself to witness. Consider your breathing, heartbeat, and relationship to the work as you concentrate on your work. Is there anything you dislike or like about your final products? Any other ideas?

caption:
【什麼是「表達性治療連續系統 (ETC)」？】
【What is the Expressive Therapies Continuum (ETC)?】

大家還記不記得前幾週分享的刮鬍泡藝術活動呢？這個活動看似簡單，其實大有玄機！因為這個活動運用了一個對表達性治療而言相當重要的理論，也就是今天要和大家分享的「表達性治療連續系統」，簡稱「ETC」。
Do you still remember the shaving cream art activity we shared a few weeks ago? This activity seems simple, but in reality, is profound! This activity is built on a very important theory for expressive therapies, which we are going to share with you today: the Expressive Therapies Continuum (ETC)

在ETC理論中，人們和表達性媒材互動的方式，可以依照認知發展複雜程度，由低到高分為：
👉動覺/感覺層次
👉知覺/情感層次
👉認知/象徵層次
以及最特殊的👉創造力層次
創造力層次不受認知程度影響，在任何一個層次都有可能發生。因此，即使是非常簡單的活動，也可以帶給參與者創造性的體驗！
In the ETC, the ways in which people interact with expressive media can be classified into four levels based on one’s cognitive development. From the most basic to the most complex are:
👉Kinesthetic/Sensory Level
👉Perceptual/Affective Level
👉Cognitive/Symbolic Level
And the most special one—
👉Creative Level
The Creative level is not affected by cognitive development and therefore can happen at all three levels of the ETC. Thus, even the simplest activity has the capacity to provide creative experiences for participants!

ETC如何運用在表達性治療中？要如何把簡單的刮鬍泡藝術活動延伸成為具有創造力的體驗？左滑圖片看更多關於ETC的分享！
How is ETC applied in expressive therapies? How can a simple shaving cream art activity be extended into a creative experience? Please swipe left to read more about ETC!

註：
雖然ETC最初是運用於視覺藝術，但也可以被應用在音樂、戲劇、舞蹈等其他形式的藝術喔！
Notes: 
Although ETC was originally used in visual arts, it can also be applied to other forms of art such as music, drama, dance, etc.

caption:
臺波波第二次訪談文～久等啦！ 
Here's our second Table & Therapist interview ~ Thank you all for waiting! 
 
這次我們邀請到Marina Strauss，美國心理諮商師、表達性藝術治療師。不僅是萊斯利大學的教授，還是其中兩位臺波波小夥伴實習地方的藝術課領導喔！ 
This time we invited Marina Strauss, an LMHC and Expressive Arts Therapist. She's not only the adjunct professor at Lesley University but also the group leader of the art class at the internship site where two of the Table team members are interning now! 
 
Marina出生在阿根廷，在布宜諾斯艾利斯大學取得心理學士學位後，在萊斯利大學獲得了表達藝術療法和心理健康諮詢的碩士學位。畢業後一直從事相關工作到現在。 
Marina Strauss was born in Argentina. She first received her BA degree in psychology from the Universidad de Buenos Aires then earned her MA in Expressive Arts Therapies and Mental Health Counseling from Lesley University. After graduation, she has been engaged in related work until now. 
 
她的工作很多元，除了開創私人諮商室“Creative Wings: Expressive Therapies and Studio”之外，也在社群機構、學校環境等等，帶領藝術團體或是舉辦藝術工作坊的活動，為不同年齡層的人提供諮商服務。 
Her work is diverse. In addition to creating her own private counseling studio, "Creative Wings: Expressive Therapies and Studio," she also leads art groups or art workshops in community organizations, school environments, etc., providing bilingual counseling services for people of all ages. 
 
Marina參與過內在家庭系統治療的培訓，她將這種方法與表達性藝術治療結合，重視正念、自我領導。她認為人們做出的所有選擇與決定，都是為了提供某些幫助。 
Marina has been trained in Internal Family Systems (IFS), which she combines with expressive arts therapy, emphasizing mindfulness and self-leadership. She believes that all the choices and decisions people made are meant to provide help in some way. 
 
「持續投入藝術，相信創作的過程，把自己帶進過程當中，並且相信藝術可以解決問題。」By Marina Strauss 
“Keep engaged in the arts, trust the creative process, bring yourself into the process, and believe that art can solve the problem.” -- Marina Strauss

caption:
今天要來分享一個大家可以做的刮鬍泡藝術活動！無論你是大人小孩或是年長者都沒有限制。材料也很簡單，超市也買得到的刮鬍泡即可。這項活動沒有太高的所謂的藝術技巧門檻，可以促進感官的體驗、訓練注意力和身體覺察等等。分享給大家！
Today we will share a shaving cream art project about kinesthetic/sensory exploration. A trip to the supermarket will get you all the materials. 
This art project requires minimal art skills, but it can improve sensory feelings, attention, and also body awareness. Here are the details:

族群適用於：2-100歲 幾乎所有族群皆可以玩！
材料：刮鬍泡、鋁箔紙、食用色素、膠帶
Population: From 2 to 100 years old. 
Materials: shaving cream, aluminum foil, food coloring, tape

準備工作：將鋁箔紙固定在平整的桌面（可用膠帶固定，以避免創作中會滑動）並準備擠刮鬍泡
Preparation work: use about 2 feet long of aluminum foil on the flat table (you can use tape to fix the corner in case the aluminum foil move during the creation) and prepare to use the shaving cream.

1. 可以先從無色刮鬍泡在鋁箔紙上或手上開始探索。接著可以將刮鬍泡放置在錫箔紙上玩耍，讓五感（看 聽 聞 摸 ）去感受刮鬍泡。在鋁箔紙上玩耍的過程，歡迎帶著一種玩樂、好奇的心態去試試看
可以思考：刮鬍泡帶來的體驗我喜不喜歡？原因可能是什麼？任何其他的想法？
Beginning with shaving cream on the foil and hand. Allow yourself to explore it, and let your senses bring you to whatever texture, smell, sound, or shape. Feel free to just bring your joyful mind and curiosity to try every possibility when playing it on the aluminum foil.
You can think about: Do I like it? If this brings you discomfort, sit with that feeling and try to identify what causes the discomfort. Any thoughts during this process?

2. 探索一段過程之後，可以加入食用色素進刮鬍泡
（有需要的話，可以幫忙參與者加顏色）
可以思考：比較前一步驟，加入顏色過後我喜歡嗎？顏色與刮鬍泡混合的過程/結果我喜歡嗎？ 任何其他的想法？
After playing for a while, you can add the food coloring to the shaving cream and see what will happen (the facilitator can help participants add colorings if needed).
You can think about: Do I like it better after adding colors? Do I enjoy the process/result after adding colors to shaving cream? Any thoughts during this process?

3. 探索過後先不用急著收拾。可以站起來看看眼前刮鬍泡作品
可以思考：在創作玩耍中身心靈的反應是什麼？你喜歡不喜歡的部分是什麼？ 任何其他的想法？
Allow yourself to look at the shaving cream art you make after the session.
You can think about: your body's reaction/emotion/feeling during the process. Which moment do you like better, and which part do you not enjoy? Any thoughts during this process and the moment after exploration?

caption:
Poiesis這個概念是表達性藝術治療（EXA）中最著名的理論之一。Poiesis源自於希臘文，代表製造和藝術創作的意思。在表達性藝術治療的定義中，當治療師和來訪者都放下對「了解事情」的期望，並能夠「順其自然」時，這個過程就是Poiesis，而來訪者也會從這個過程中受益。 
One of the most well-known theories in expressive arts therapy (EXA) is the concept of poiesis. Poiesis is grounded in the practice of EXA, a Greek word for creating and art-making. In EXA, poiesis represents a process that benefits the client when the therapist and client let go of the expectation of knowing and “let it be.”  
-
在表達性藝術治療實務工作中，治療師與來訪者一起使用多種藝術形式，陪伴來訪者“脫離”現實，進入想像──Poiesis 的世界。在這裡，新的符號、圖像、資源和以前未被發現的可能性可以被發現，並解決來訪者現實生活中的問題和困難。通過洞察與解鎖，來訪者開始看到他們在生活中改變和轉變的可能性。在這個未知世界中，我們探索一切可能發生的任何事情，發現以前隱藏在黑暗中的寶藏。 
By using multiple art modalities with the clients, the therapist accompanies the clients to “decenter” from reality and enters the imaginative world. This is the world of poiesis, where new symbols, images, resources, and previously undiscovered possibilities can be found to resolve issues and difficulties in a client’s life in reality. By witnessing this unfolding in this world, the clients begin seeing the possibility for change and transformation in their lives. In this unknown world, we explore whatever may come our way and discover treasures previously concealed in the dark. 
-
因此，藝術創作是進入Poiesis的橋樑。Poiesis是表達性藝術的方式，一種遊走想像世界的方式。當踏上通往未知領域的道路時，我們會獲得看待自己和世界的新視角，和它們的真實面貌。透過藝術創作，我們在想像世界和現實之間穿梭，帶回我們需要的真相，讓現實生活中獲得自由和治癒。我把這個真相想像成一盞溫暖的覺醒之光，讓我們更接近內在的完整性。
Thus, art-making is the bridge to enter the realm of poiesis. Poiesis is the way of expressive arts, a way of wandering in the imaginative world. By taking a road to undiscovered territory, we gain a new perspective and truth about ourselves and the world as we wander. Through art-making, we travel between the imaginative and literal world, bringing back the truth we need to set us free and heal in real life. I imagine this truth as a warm awakening light, bringing us closer to inner wholeness.

Here comes the first Table & Therapist Interview!

這次訪問到的是美國音樂治療師 Wendy Krueger，是臺波波其中一個小夥伴的實習督導喔！
We invited Wendy Krueger, a board-certified music therapist, who is also the internship supervisor of one of our Table Expressive Therapies members!
-
自2006年在Berklee音樂學院拿到音樂治療學位後，Wendy 就一直從事音樂治療到現在。
Wendy has been practicing music therapy since getting her degree in music therapy at Berklee College of Music in 2006.

Wendy目前是美國麻州東北部私人音樂治療工作室Up Beat Music Therapy的負責人，主要的服務對象有長者、失智症患者、成人精神疾病患者、身心障礙成人。
Wendy is currently the director of Up Beat Music Therapy, a private practice in Northeastern Massachusetts. She works with elders, adults with memory loss, adults in psych units, and adults with intellectual and developmental disabilities. 
-
身為一名音樂治療師，Wendy非常重視人與人之間的關係，以及每個人獨特的優勢和資源。
As a music therapist, Wendy places great emphasis on building relationships with people and the unique strengths and resources of each individual.

🎵「在我的音樂治療中，一個很大的目標是『正常化』，讓參與者有機會去感覺到他們和一般人是無異的；在音樂裡，他們能夠暫時地、單純地做個人類。」 by Wendy 音樂治療師
🎵“A big goal in my music therapy is ‘normalization’, giving participants the opportunity to feel like they are normal like everyone else. Music is an opportunity for them to just be human beings for a little while,” says Wendy. 
-
身為執業多年的音樂治療師，Wendy對音樂治療有什麼體悟？有什麼話想告訴對音樂治療有興趣的大家？訪談內容都在圖片中，左滑即可觀看Wendy的分享喔！

大家有沒有過這樣的經驗呢？聽到某一首歌，就想起某一段時光；或是相反，當想起某一段時光，腦海裡就浮現某一段旋律。 

音樂具有承載與喚起記憶的功能，因而與我們的生命經驗息息相關。我在Lesley上的第一堂課的第一個作業，就是要創造屬於自己的「音樂自傳 (Music autobiography) 」。創造音樂自傳不需要任何音樂背景或專業訓練，只需將自己的人生分成數個階段，並回想和思考哪些歌曲能代表各個時期。舉例而言，也許幼時每晚聽著入睡的搖籃曲代表童年，某一首情歌代表青澀的初戀⋯⋯。在這個過程中，或許會忽然想起：「啊！原來當時曾經發生過這樣的事啊！」「原來當時我有這樣的感覺啊！」那些大大小小的經驗、事件、感受與想法，都是值得被重視的。 

在此和大家分享我的音樂自傳中的其中一首歌：美國搖滾樂團Hinder的Homecoming Queen
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wkG56P9uBeU

大家的音樂自傳中有什麼樣的歌曲呢？歡迎留言和我們分享喔！ 
 
（小提醒：音樂可能會喚起許多情緒與感受。在創造和聆聽音樂自傳時，請允許自己適時休息一下喔！） 

Have you ever had such an experience when you heard a piece of music and were transported back to a particular moment? Or conversely, when you recalled a certain period of time in your life, a certain melody emerged in your mind? 
 
Music has the function of carrying and evoking memories. Thus, music is inseparable from our life experiences. The first assignment for the first course that I took at Lesley University was to create my own “music autobiography.” Creating a music autobiography does not require one to have any musical background or professional training. All you need to do is to divide your life into multiple phases, then recall and think about which songs represent each period of time. For example, a lullaby that you listened to every night as a baby may represent your childhood, and a specific love song may represent your first love. 
 
During the process of creating a music autobiography, some faded memories and feelings may suddenly appear in your mind: “Ah! So this actually happened at that time!” “So I actually had this feeling at that time!” Those events, emotions, feelings, and thoughts that you have experienced in your life are all worth valuing. 
 
Here I would like to share with you one of the songs in my music autobiography: Homecoming Queen by Hinder. 
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wkG56P9uBeU
 
What kind of songs do you have in your music autobiography? Please leave a comment below and share with us! 
 
(Tips: Music may evoke many emotions and feelings so please allow yourself to take a break from time to time when creating or listening to a music autobiography🙂)
